Prognostic Discussion for 6 to 10 and 8 to 14 day outlooks
NWS Climate Prediction Center College Park, MD
300 PM EST Fri November 13 2026

6-10 DAY OUTLOOK FOR NOV 19 - 23 2026

Dynamical ensemble guidance from the GEFS, ECENS, and CMCE, are in good 
agreement on the 5 day mean 500-hPa height pattern during the 6 to 10 day 
period. Positive 500-hPa height anomalies are favored from eastern and central 
Alaska across most of Canada into the eastern contiguous U.S. (CONUS). Negative 
500-hPa height anomalies are forecast for most of the western CONUS (except for 
the northern tier) and western Alaska into the Bering Sea. Daily model guidance 
indicates a mid-level low over the West Coast early in the period progressing 
inland with another trough following behind, although this second area of 
negative anomalies is unlikely to make it to the West Coast by day 10. The 
first area of mid-level low pressure is forecast to eject into the Plains by 
days 8 and 9. Near Alaska, the GEFS has trended more towards the ECENS with a 
ridge axis across western Canada.

Above normal temperatures are forecast across most of the CONUS east of the 
Rocky Mountains as a result of mid-level high pressure across much of the 
eastern CONUS early in the period. The highest probabilities for above normal 
temperatures, greater than 80%, are over the Great Lakes region. Odds are 
reduced across portions of the Southeast and Gulf Coast with lower height 
anomalies and mid-level troughing progressing into the region with time. Over 
most of the West, below normal temperatures are favored with mid-level low 
pressure moving across the region during the 6-10 day period. In Alaska, above 
normal temperatures are likely over most of the state with the highest degree 
of confidence over the eastern Mainland. Meanwhile, in Hawaii, above normal 
temperatures are favored over the Big Island with near normal favored across 
the remainder of the island chain. 

Above normal precipitation is favored from California through much of the 
Rockies and into the Plains and Mississippi Valley associated with mid-level 
low pressure progressing across the southern tier and cyclogenesis in the lee 
of the Rockies. There is some uncertainty with the track of any area of low 
pressure that may form as the GEFS takes the low towards the Great Lakes while 
the ECENS tracks the low into the Middle-Mississippi Valley. A more southern 
route would favor drier conditions over the Upper Mississippi Valley. Below 
normal precipitation is favored over the northeastern CONUS ahead of any 
precipitation from the eastward moving system. Below normal is also favored for 
portions of the Northwest closer to mid-level ridging. In Alaska, near to below 
normal precipitation is favored for Southeast Alaska, while above normal is 
favored over the Mainland. In Hawaii, below normal precipitation is favored for 
the island chain, consistent with consolidation tools and the winter El Nino 
signal.

The official 6-10 day 500-hPa height blend consists of 10% of Today's 0z GFS 
Ensemble Mean centered on Day 8, 25% of Today's 6z GFS Ensemble Mean centered 
on Day 8, 40% of Today's 0z European Ensemble Mean centered on Day 8, and 25% 
of Today's 0z Canadian Ensemble Mean centered on Day 8 
 

FORECAST CONFIDENCE FOR THE 6-10 DAY PERIOD: Above Normal, 4 out 5, Good 
agreement among the dynamical model, heights, temperatures, and precipitation 
forecast is offset slightly by concerns regarding lee-side cyclogenesis. 

8-14 DAY OUTLOOK FOR NOV 21 - 27 2026 

The week-2 ensemble forecasts from the GEFS, ECENS, and CMCE are again in fair 
agreement, particularly over the CONUS, for the forecast 7 day mean 500-hPa 
height pattern. Positive anomalies are again forecast across Canada and into 
the northeastern CONUS. The mid-level low pressure initially over the West 
Coast in the 6-10 day period, is undercutting this ridge bringing below normal 
500-hPa heights to much of the southern tier of the CONUS. In Alaska, there are 
some differences but with better agreement among the models today relative to 
yesterday. The GEFS has trended weaker and east with a mid-level ridge axis 
bringing it into better agreement with the ECENS and CMCE that forecast a ridge 
axis over western Canada.

Above normal temperatures are favored across most of the eastern CONUS during 
week-2 as a result of mid-level high pressure across much of the eastern and 
northern CONUS. The highest probabilities are over the Great Lakes, Northeast, 
and Mid-Atlantic with probabilities for above normal temperatures exceeding 
60%. Odds are reduced across portions of the Southeast and Gulf Coast with a 
mid-level trough moving into the south-central CONUS with time. Near to below 
normal temperatures are favored over parts of the Great Basin, Four Corners, 
and Southern Plains behind the southern stream troughing feature. Warming 
temperatures are favored across California and Oregon from the 6-10 day period 
with a slight tilt towards above normal forecast across the entirety of the 
West Coast during week-2. In Alaska, above normal temperatures are likely over 
most of the state with the highest degree of confidence over the eastern 
Mainland. Meanwhile, in Hawaii, above normal temperatures are favored for the 
Big Island, below normal temperatures are favored for Kauai, and near normal is 
favored for the islands in between. 

Above normal precipitation is favored for much of California with mid-level 
troughing offshore potentially bringing some additional precipitation into the 
state during week-2. Below normal precipitation is favored for the Pacific 
Northwest, the northern Rockies, and the northern Great Basin. Some tools bring 
this below normal precipitation into parts of the Four Corners but others favor 
above. As a result, near normal precipitation is favored in this region. Above 
normal precipitation is favored for much of the Plains and Mississippi Valley 
associated with mid-level low pressure progressing across the southern tier and 
lee-side cyclogenesis. A greater than 50% chance of above normal precipitation 
is forecast for southern Texas and into Florida with a southern stream trough 
progressing across the region. Near to above normal precipitation is favored 
for the northeastern CONUS consistent with most of the tools and elevated 
uncertainty regarding the path of any storm system leading into Thanksgiving. 
Near normal precipitation is favored for Southeast Alaska, while near to above 
normal is generally favored over much of the Mainland. In Hawaii, below normal 
precipitation is favored for the island chain, consistent with consolidation 
tools and the winter El Nino signal.

The official 8-14 day 500-hPa height blend consists of: 10% of Today's 0z GFS 
Ensemble Mean centered on Day 11, 30% of Today's 6z GFS Ensemble Mean centered 
on Day 11, 40% of Today's 0z European Ensemble Mean centered on Day 11, and 20% 
of Today's 0z Canadian Ensemble Mean centered on Day 11 


FORECAST CONFIDENCE FOR THE 8-14 DAY PERIOD: Above Normal, 4 out 5, Good 
agreement among the dynamical model, heights, temperatures, and precipitation 
forecast is offset slightly by concerns regarding lee-side cyclogenesis. 

FORECASTER: Ryan Bolt

Notes:


The notation for the categorical forecast indicated on the maps is 
the same as that in the tables: A-above   N-near normal   B-below 
 
The temperature map shows regions with > 33% chance of being warmer
(orange, "A"), colder (blue, "B"), or close to (gray, "N") normal.
Labels on the shaded lines give the probability (> 33%) of the more
likely category (B or A). Probability of N is always < 40%.
 
The precipitation map shows regions with > 33% chance of being 
wetter (green, "A"), drier (tan, "B"), or close to (gray, "N")
normal. Labels on the shaded lines give the probability (> 33%) of
the more likely category (B or A). Probability of N is always < 40%.
 
In the southwest and other climatologically dry regions - there will 
be a greater than 33.3% chance of no precipitation and occasionally 
even a normal (i.e. Median) value of zero - especially during the dry 
seasons.  In such cases a forecast of near normal is effectively a 
forecast of little or no precipitation. 
 
The climate prediction center uses 1991-2020 base period means as  
reference in the climate outlooks.

The next set of long-lead monthly and seasonal outlooks will be released on 
November 19.
